result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another, from other species, and from the Earth itself.

This shift would dissolve the roots of greed, conflict, and exploitation, because harming another (or the planet) would be as unthinkable as harming oneself. Empathy would become the default, not the exception. Systems of oppression, environmental destruction, and short-term thinking would collapse under the weight of this realization.

It wouldn’t erase difference or individuality—those are beautiful—but it would make cooperation as natural as breathing. The world wouldn’t become "perfect," but it would finally have a chance to heal.

(And then, of course, I’d ask for a second wish to give everyone good coffee. Priorities.)
